outcome.technical: A subject's run record reaches every reader only through _evidence_io.project_record, through one table (RECORD_GRAMMAR); the writer's one egress, finished_record, stores through stored_record over the same table, and _record_of writes gateSource from the row's scope. A holder (a task whole, or a phase outside its tasks) writing any key twice holds no readable record (holder_duplicate_problem), and run-test-gate refuses to rewrite such a file, naming the hand step. reusable_run repeats nothing over a newer run the same subject holds under another identity or gate (_newer_holder_run). close-phase refuses when a ref does not resolve and none holds the plan; the release guard says a missing shard does not exist. Round 4: rf3 (every required field at every depth), rf4 (an unnamed key at every depth, neither stored nor projected) and ho8 (a task's doubled key leaves its phase's record readable) cover the reviewer's surviving mutations n39, n36 and n34; vm3 and vb-base1/vb-base2 had become vacuous since the projection made their fixture record unreadable (a null baseRed.run, a shape the writer's row_for never stores), now fixed and each asserting the record reads and its kept base run reaches the selection. Docs narrowed: run-test-gate alone refuses a doubled key, the plan's other writers still save the last copy, validate-manifest does not warn on a doubled phase tasks key, SECURITY.md carries the timing command without a number. Worktree, after the last edit: gate-parity exit 0; task sweep 10/10 files, 3556 cases, exit 0; dependant sweep 19/19 files, 3726 cases, exit 0; full sweep 198/198 files, 19811 cases, exit 0; ruff and vermin exit 0; mutation table 54/54 caught on scratch copies. The red-first command runs tests/test__evidence_io.py alone, because the helper's house reader takes one tally (the last N/M line) and two suites in one output would be graded by the second; vm1 is proved red by mutation row 3 (own_runs reads the newest readable row), vm3 by rows 49 and 50 (one selection taking a task's kept base run; own_runs dropping its base-scope filter), which also redden vb-base1/vb-base2; vm2 is the oracle beside vm1 and holds green by design. CI: 44686964116 (round 1) and 44699803319 (round 2) green on every job; round 3's 44738645013 green on every job after one rerun of browser (report), which had been cut at its time bound; round 4 changed only tests and documents. Independent reads: read 1's findings were fixed in round 2; read 2 found M1-M4 and L1-L4 (the projection, a holder writing its record key twice, the subject's newest run deciding reuse, a CHANGELOG over-claim, the guard's missing shard, m21/m24/m28/m29), all confirmed fixed by read 3 with its own probes; read 3 found three tests that could not fail (n34, n36, n39, now ho8, rf4, rf3, each proven red) and four document over-claims (narrowed), and moved the plan's one parse/save door (_manifest_io saving one copy of a doubled key; a doubled phase tasks key) to P169.32-6l3. Dependants: guard-release and arm-release-bypass read the plan through the same parse and pass in the gate and dependant sweeps; the importers of _evidence_io, run-test-gate, _verdict_binding, close-phase and drive-phase pass in those sweeps and the full sweep; PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE, SECURITY.md and CHANGELOG were edited to say what the tree does; docs/research/guard-ownership-design.md is a draft outside this task and was not touched.
outcome.descriptive: A run record is read only as the writer writes it, so no older run answers for a subject whose own record cannot be read.
